answer: A stake-weighted reputation vault raises the cost of Sybil attacks: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, and the deposit grows with the volume it wants to move. A newcomer starts on a small knoll of trust, earning credit only through verified deliveries, while a fake identity that burns its deposit loses more than it gains. Like a pearl forming layer by layer, reputation accrues slowly and cannot be faked in bulk, so spinning up thousands of sock-puppet agents costs thousands of locked deposits with no shortcut to influence.
